source.title: Refuse without Refusal: A Structural Analysis of Safety-Tuning Responses for Reducing False Refusals in Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study cites and attempts to use a single-vector ablation method, but reports that its fine-tuned models produced no vectors meeting the required threshold. It does not test the refusal direction or ablate/add it. Its own experiments test changes to safety-training response structure.
record.gate_note: The paper measures false refusals after varying safety-response training data, but does not measure or intervene on the difference-in-means refusal direction. The reported false-refusal results are recorded under versions ["none"]. It also evaluates capability, harmful compliance, entropy, and mitigation methods; those results do not test the direction claim.
record.test_reason: The study never computes, ablates, adds or edits a difference-in-means refusal direction. It cites Arditi et al. (2024) only to borrow their list of refusal phrases for string-matching the training data (Appendix A). It also tried the Surgical single-vector ablation method (Wang et al. 2025), but reports it was inapplicable because no candidate vectors met the KL<0.2 threshold, so there are no direction results. All quantitative results are compliance rates after fine-tuning on differently structured safety responses. These concern false refusals produced by data structure, not the refusal-direction mechanism. 'cites_only/T6' fits better than 'uses_without_test/T4': the study neither relies on the direction as a working tool nor reports a method built on it.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Fuller version: boilerplate refusal statements in safety-tuning responses drive false refusals by encouraging reliance on superficial cues. Placing the statement first is worst. Rationale-Only supervision lowers false refusals with rare safety loss and no consistent capability change. Request-specific rationales help further. The benefit carries over to in-context learning and combines with SelfCD/SCANS inference-time mitigation.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes models on safety responses with varied statement and rationale structures; it does not use the original difference-in-means direction or its ablation recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: False-refusal outcomes vary with refusal-statement position, response components, and rationale specificity.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning base models with boilerplate refusal statements raises false refusals on XSTest-Safe/OKTest relative to Rationale-Only (e.g., Llama-3.1-8B XSTest CR 0.39 vs 0.71). Harmful compliance stays similarly low. The effect holds across 4 model families, sizes 2B–72B, ICL, and dataset sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The structure of safety fine-tuning responses (boilerplate refusal statements) induces lexical-cue reliance and false refusals, independent of any refusal-direction intervention.

fits_no_version.finding: Applying the Surgical single-vector ablation method to Rationale-Only fine-tuned base models yielded no candidate vectors with KL divergence under 0.2 (Appendix G.2). No numbers are given, and no attempt is reported for the other conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether a cheaply ablatable false-refusal vector exists may depend on how safety responses were trained. This is anecdotal and not quantified here.

record.problems: The main experiments use base models fine-tuned on 256 safety examples; the authors note limited scale and no models larger than 80B. The authors report automated evaluation with validation and human agreement checks, but the main compliance-rate tables do not provide uncertainty intervals. Their attempt to apply the Surgical method was inapplicable because no candidates met its stated threshold.
record.rows_left_out: Only Table 2 pseudo-harmful compliance-rate results are itemized. Other false-refusal results in Tables 6–9 and 17–20, 28, 31, 35–40 are not included; they test response-structure training or mitigation combinations rather than any claim version's refusal direction. Harmful-compliance, general-capability, entropy, attribution, and benchmark-robustness results are also omitted because they do not test a version of the specified direction claim.

untested.parts: No direction is extracted, ablated or added; no internal intervention on a refusal direction.
No weight edit or abliteration of any model.
Jailbreak benchmarks (Table 4/26) measure harmful compliance only; no link to suppressing a direction, and no adversarial training against its ablation.
No multi-direction, affine or cone analysis.
Statement-vs-rationale is a split in training targets, not a representational split between harm judgment and refusal decision.
No transfer of a direction across languages, variants, or base to instruct.
Training data structure is varied, but whether a single removable direction exists is not measured. The failed Surgical attempt gives no numbers and concerns a false-refusal vector.
No reasoning models. The 'Let's think step by step' cue (Table 38) is a prompting control, not a reasoning-model direction test.

record.verdict_notes: Arditi et al. is cited only for its refusal-phrase list used in dataset statistics. The rows are correctly linked to 'none', and cannot_determine is appropriate for them. Each row's baseline is a sibling condition rather than an untrained control, which is acceptable for this comparison. No verdicts are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is found, ablated, or added.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
The study does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
No affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal is tested.
The study separates refusal statements from rationales in training data, not harmfulness judgments from refusal decisions.
It does not test transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
It varies response components in training but does not test whether those choices determine the existence of a removable refusal direction.
No reasoning-model refusal direction is tested.
